title: Capability execution ledger
status_policy: OpenBMT capability completion and exact benchmark parity are tracked separately. A row becomes verified_supported when the current product exposes the canonical merchant job and meaningful source, test or observed-workflow evidence validates it. Vendor-specific mechanisms and qualifiers remain open under benchmark_parity_status until separately demonstrated. Planning phases and adjacent primitives never close a row by themselves.
execution_context: The native foundations batch is implemented as seven bounded, locally validated candidates. A two-axis audit closes seven canonical OpenBMT merchant capabilities while retaining every linked benchmark qualifier as a separate open obligation. Next independent work includes staff authority, catalog/pricing configuration, shift/refund reconciliation and Bitcoin receiving/recovery; shared contracts and cross-cutting safety gates still apply. This ledger sequences work and is not new competitor research.
workstream_order: P3 parallel Bitcoin safety/readiness/recovery after shared gates
P5 later verticals after standalone-shift evidence

phase_definitions.GATE-SALE-01: Shared gate: canonical durable sale, exact-money pricing snapshot, tender-attempt identity and interruption/recovery contracts reviewed. This is a prerequisite milestone, not a capability completion claim.
phase_definitions.GATE-AUTH-01: Shared gate: owner/staff/device/integration authority matrix and independent recovery rules reviewed. This is a prerequisite milestone, not a capability completion claim.
phase_definitions.P1: Standalone sale foundation, pricing, catalog, stock and tender work. Active start: native durable priced-sale snapshot.
phase_definitions.P2: Staff, cash operations, customer operations, reporting and complete shift work after the minimal sale/tender contract exists.
phase_definitions.P3: Bitcoin safety, readiness and recovery track. Runs in parallel with P1/P2 once GATE-SALE-01 and GATE-AUTH-01 are met; safety gates apply to every phase.
phase_definitions.P4: Optional provider and hardware qualification. Can proceed after shared sale/authority contracts; never a prerequisite for cash/direct Bitcoin operation.
phase_definitions.P5: Later vertical, online and multi-location jobs after a validated standalone shift. Deferral preserves these jobs in backlog.

decision_gate_policy: Rows carry research_decision_ids as an overlay independent of delivery workstream. Linked decisions are proposed constraints/mechanisms with proof or revisit triggers in the source decision register; resolve the applicable gate before implementing the affected mechanism. This preserves the underlying merchant job.
cross_cutting_safety_gates: Do not represent Bitcoin as settled while observation/readiness is stale or absent.
Keep merchant Bitcoin funds authority independent from card/provider access and company service permission.
Do not make a second collection safe after unknown payment outcomes without reconciling the original attempt.
Preserve durable sale, tender, refund, stock and closeout identity through restart/recovery before fulfillment or payout.
Apply least privilege and auditable owner approval to spending, destination changes, refunds, exports and staff actions.
Treat simulation, UI, documentation, adjacent primitives and candidate evidence as non-closure until the row-specific acceptance boundary is met.

implementation_candidates.status_policy: These entries map only jobs touched by the current native diff. Their row-level ledger statuses remain pending_unverified. Candidate status in_progress_unverified is not acceptance, validation, completion, support, or parity. Scoped local tests and observed device workflows are recorded in candidate evidence; they do not establish the full benchmark capability or remove its unmet boundaries.
implementation_candidates.evidence_source_note: Exact implementation file paths are relative to the openbmt-acceptance-research repository. Capability and benchmark IDs link back to the retained register; the historical corpus is unchanged.

candidates.feature_cluster: Frozen priced sale, total calculation and receipt projection
candidates.supported_subset: Android native code now has integer-minor-unit pricing inputs and a frozen snapshot; bounded USD pricing supports one flat inclusive or exclusive basket tax, fixed order discount allocation, optional tip, catalog-selected variant/modifier amounts, durable sale storage, and receipt/report projections. Checkout UI exposes discount, tax-rate, tip and pricing preview before freezing the priced sale.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Implementation candidate only. Current source limits pricing to USD and one flat basket tax; no jurisdiction selection, tax calculation responsibility, tax exemptions, compounding, line-level tax differences, percent/item discounts, discount policy, saved pricing configuration, or broad modifier administration. Scoped tests/device observations are recorded in candidate evidence; variant-specific competitor qualifiers and full receipt workflow remain open.

candidates.feature_cluster: Local catalog create/edit/archive, single-variant item workflow and lookup
candidates.supported_subset: Native local catalog persists immutable revisions; current management UI can add/edit/archive products with one variant, exact USD price, optional SKU/barcode, search by name/identifier, and manually enter a SKU/barcode to find an item.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Candidate only; scoped local validation is recorded in candidate evidence and full capability acceptance remains open. Current UI creates one-variant products and edits a selected variant and does not configure modifier definitions. Code lookup is typed/manual; no camera, physical scanner, scanner recovery or device qualification. No bulk import/export, provider catalog, full menu/catalog administration, or parity claim.

candidates.feature_cluster: Local stock mode, count adjustment and sale-linked fulfillment decrement
candidates.supported_subset: Native code provides tracked/manual stock modes, opening count, reasoned adjustments with expected-version checks, and idempotent fulfillment tied to a stable eligible sale version; tracked inventory decrements through that fulfillment record.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Candidate only; scoped local validation is recorded in candidate evidence and full capability acceptance remains open. This is not purchasing, vendor management, stock transfer, cycle/full count approval, multi-location stock, automatic fulfillment policy, or demonstrated physical handoff. Fulfillment eligibility is bounded and may require a separate operator action.

candidates.feature_cluster: Manual cash session, movements, count and discrepancy record
candidates.supported_subset: Native journal models opening float, manual cash-in/out with reason/operator label, explicit linking of recorded sale cash payments, expected balance, operator-entered close count and immutable discrepancy/history.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Candidate only; scoped local validation is recorded in candidate evidence and full capability acceptance remains open. Operator labels are unauthenticated. No physical drawer read/control, blind close, enforced role permissions, paid-in/out verification, tips/employee payouts, full tender-aware Z report, business-day policy, or accounting-grade closeout is established. A cash session count is not proof a physical drawer was counted correctly.

candidates.feature_cluster: Local date-range tender-aware report and CSV export
candidates.supported_subset: Read-only report aggregates local ledger sales by creation-date range in device timezone; shows observed/applied tender amounts, payment states, refund requests/payments, known pricing components, and supports reviewed CSV copy/save.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Candidate only; scoped local validation is recorded in candidate evidence and full capability acceptance remains open. Report is not a shift close, cashbook, staff report or accounting-compliance export. No staff identities/authentication or staff grouping, refund cash-flow-by-date, accounting integration, independently reconciled report correctness, or export permission model.

candidates.feature_cluster: Receipt pricing detail in the native sale view
candidates.supported_subset: Native receipt projection includes item lines, selected modifier amount labels where present, frozen subtotal/discount/tax/tip and total, tender observations, and existing sale state distinctions.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Candidate only; scoped local validation is recorded in candidate evidence and full capability acceptance remains open. No physical receipt printer, customer email/SMS delivery, configurable receipt template, device matrix, full return/refund receipt lifecycle, or observed cashier usability is established.

candidates.feature_cluster: Advisory Shop Lightning receiving snapshot, capacity and backup-state visibility
candidates.supported_subset: Shop Lightning report/protocol now carries a receiving snapshot with estimated confirmed capacity, pending/unknown channels, confirmation depth, chain status, counter-reported second-copy state and pending write counts. Owner UI treats absent, stale or future-dated snapshots as unknown; amount-specific fee/route status remains explicitly not checked.
candidates.unmet_boundary: Candidate only; scoped local validation is recorded in candidate evidence and full capability acceptance remains open. Snapshot is advisory and does not prove inbound route, amount-specific fee, guaranteed readiness, backup independence, successful restore, peer-loss recovery or safe channel exit. Counter clock is not verified by phone. No provider/hardware qualification or complete merchant receiving journey is established.

explicit_nonclaims: No broad product category or untouched row is inferred implemented.
Staff authority is still absent: operator/staff labels are unauthenticated and do not enforce roles or permissions.
Physical devices, card provider approval/production integration, multi-location workflows, online/restaurant vertical workflows, and hardware qualification are untouched by these candidate mappings.
Model tests, implementation code and partial native UI are not POS parity or observed acceptance evidence.
